name: Patient Health Questionnaire-4 (PHQ-4)
description: The four-item PHQ-4 ultra-brief screener for anxiety and depressive symptoms over the past two weeks, with standard response options and scoring metadata.
source: Kroenke, Spitzer, Williams, and Löwe (2009), An ultra-brief screening scale for anxiety and depression: the PHQ-4.
license: PHQ and GAD instruments were released by Pfizer without copyright restriction and at no charge. Preserve instrument wording and cite the developers.
intended_use: Ultra-brief adult research screening for core anxiety and depressive symptoms. It is not a diagnosis, crisis assessment, or momentary EMA measure.
validation_status: Established adult screening instrument. The shared two-week prompt is repeated in each item for mobile presentation; item content and response coding are otherwise preserved. A positive screen requires appropriate research or clinical follow-up procedures.

measure.scoring: Code Not at all=0, Several days=1, More than half the days=2, Nearly every day=3. Sum all four items for 0–12 total distress (0–2 none, 3–5 mild, 6–8 moderate, 9–12 severe). Items 1–2 form GAD-2 and items 3–4 form PHQ-2; each subscale ranges 0–6, with 3 or greater commonly used as a positive screen. Follow the cited source for interpretation.

references.note: Primary rights-holder statement that the PHQ and GAD instruments are available without copyright restriction and at no charge.

references.label: Kroenke et al. (2009), Psychosomatics
references.note: Original PHQ-4 development and validation report.

questions.text: Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by not being able to stop or control worrying?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you been bothered by little interest or pleasure in doing things?
